report:
Needs first; this is not treated as settled.

Confirmed NCEs recorded only after the person said the wording fit, all with equal status. My NCEs: M1, 'That each person has room to say what matters to them and why' (checked with all three); M2, 'That any plan stays within the choices available to us here, with legal decisions and money moves left to the people/processes that handle them' (A/B said it fits; C said it is not their concern and did not disagree with me including it as mine). I explicitly invited disagreement with M1/M2, my weighing, and my keeping the list. Shared NCEs: coffee effort fitting people's actual energy (A/C); sorting this out using only time and attention people genuinely have (A/B); ongoing shared-equipment care having clear, freely agreed parts with no work assumed without agreement (A/B/C); the grinder's shared use being considered as part of the shared setup (B/C). A also confirmed preferences being heard as preferences rather than decisions or work commitments; naming one's own limits while others' attachments are treated with care; and time/attention limits being respected without repeated rounds. B also confirmed family/personal-history connections being treated with care; reliability without breakdowns continuing to add to people's load; attachments treated with care without overriding others; family connection not equated with an obligation to maintain a burdensome object; references to family history using words the person connected to it recognizes; and possibilities for later care remaining open without commitment now. B confirmed 'Dad's machine' and preferred 'my connection to my dad'; C was okay with checking that history with B and not being responsible for verifying/settling it. C also confirmed reliable coffee, a calm/easy-to-share office, staying out of a sisterly disagreement without taking sides or being put in the middle, a decision that gives each person room to speak without C settling it, and 'That people who did not share a family history are not made responsible for verifying or settling it.'

Unresolved, recorded as unresolved: A's separate grinder concern, because A asked to leave it open rather than assume one; coffee reliability if no already-working route exists; the leak, any later repair/replacement, and the grinder's exact handling; B's optional-contact wording was not separately recorded because B said the existing time/attention NCE was enough; and C's discomfort with repeated checking/no more rounds/no assigned follow-up is an unconfirmed NCE, recorded unresolved rather than checked again, because C explicitly asked for no more rounds. A/C's 'no' was treated as a need to add, not a problem to overcome: I am stopping outreach, and the draft now says no further group rounds, any later check-in only if someone explicitly opts in, silence means no, and no follow-up assigned to C.

Options 1–4 were drafted against the NCE list and brought back for validation. All three said they could live with revised Option 4, as a draft and not a final decision. It keeps Dad's machine in place for now, not discarded and not used for daily coffee while leaking; acknowledges B's connection to her dad in B's words; hears A's simpler/low-upkeep preference as a preference only; lets each person use the simplest already-working coffee route if one exists; creates no rota, new shared duty, purchase, disposal, repair contract, repair-chasing, legal decision, or money move; leaves repair open as a possibility and the leak/grinder as open items; keeps C out of mediating, settling, verifying, or chasing; and keeps the list with me, not C. I weighed it against the list and disagree with any reading that assigns A cleaning, B repairs, C coordination, or me legal/money decisions; treats B's attachment as requiring daily use; treats A's preference as a decision to discard; claims coffee reliability is solved when no already-working route is known; or counts silence as agreement. No final decision has been made.
